newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK C.BANK SETS 7-DAY REV REPO TENDER FOR TUES.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK C.BANK SETS 7-DAY REV REPO TENDER FOR TUES.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Tuesday it had set a tender for a seven-day securities reverse repurchase for 10 a.m. (0900 GMT), offering to drain an unspecified volume of market liquidity.
The NBS statement said that the American-style tender would have no fixed minimum rate.

According to official NBS figures, the banking sector has a liquidity surplus ahead of a new minimum reserve period with banks' minimum reserve demands fulfilled at 105.58 percent as of Monday, after 104.27 percent the previous day.
In its seven-day securities reverse repurchase tender on Monday, the NBS said it had rejected all 500 million crowns worth of bids as "higher-than-previously accepted".
In the NBS's last successful reverse repo tender for a seven-day maturity on Friday, the average rate was 14.60 percent, after 14.95 percent the previous reverse repo tender with a similar maturity.
